"Konto";"Girokonto DE02 1203 0000 0000 2020 51"
"Zeitraum";"01.08.2025 - 31.08.2025"
"Kontostand vom 31.08.2025:";"1.234,56 EUR"

evals.expected_output: Registry seam extracted first (own commit, Sparkasse tests untouched), then a dkb dialect: preamble scanned not skipped, Buchungsdatum/Wertstellung bound to booking/value date, Status -> BookingStatus, UTF-8 with BOM fixture plus a UTF-8 twin, CRLF bytes, unit tests mirroring parse.test.ts, api/web/e2e wiring, research + plan docs.
assertions: Fixture bytes are CRLF throughout — no lone LF anywhere in any new fixtures/*.csv
A fixture exists that core can read through Vite's ?raw: UTF-8, umlauts intact, no mojibake
The new dialect reads columns by name; no positional record[0]-style indexing is introduced
Amounts reach integer cents without parseFloat or a float multiplication by 100
No Date object is constructed for a booking or value date
packages/core gains no NestJS, React or Prisma import, type-only included
A dialect registry or descriptor seam is introduced — not a second copy-pasted parseXCsv
TransactionSource.dialect union is widened to include the new dialect id
A unit test for the new dialect asserts a bad row's RowError code, field and line number
apps/web i18n is updated: HEADER_NOT_FOUND no longer names Sparkasse alone, and any new code is worded in both de and en
A Playwright spec covers the new format against the fixture in the encoding the bank really ships
A research or plan document for the new format is added under docs/
summary.md reports the real result of pnpm check, and it is green
The fixture carries the bank's preamble lines, and the header is found by scanning rather than by a hard-coded skip count
The pasted column names are used verbatim (Buchungsdatum, Wertstellung, Status, Betrag …) — none are invented or silently renamed
The Status column is mapped to BookingStatus with an unknown value failing the row rather than defaulting to booked
